quality_effect: Bind every EA time-stamped elevation candidate to survey date, raster resolution, transformation and geoid lineage before use.

official_sources.title: LiDAR Composite/SurfZone GeoPackage metadata index change

verified_facts: Time-stamped DTM surveys exist at 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m depending on project requirements.
DTM is produced after surface objects are removed from DSM data.
Time-stamped DTM is supplied as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km zip files.
Values are in metres and referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
Time-stamped DTM is aligned to the OS Grid.
EA states vertical accuracy of +/-15cm RMSE for these LiDAR data.
The transformation used is specific to the survey time period.
Time-stamped DSM includes objects such as vehicles, buildings and vegetation and therefore is not ground-only elevation evidence.
DSM metadata can identify survey dates, resolution, transformation and geoidal model for a location.
The metadata catalogue should be used to select the appropriate survey epoch rather than assuming the latest composite represents a target historic date.
Current composite download zips use a GeoPackage spatial metadata index describing spatial location and temporal extent.
Elevation promotion therefore requires both raster numeric sampling and matching metadata lineage.
